name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 162 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 20% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 162 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 20 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Security forces in Jammu and Kashmir are conducting high-level reviews of winter security and citizen-centric policing, while six militants were killed in recent encounters and senior officials such as the Home Secretary and the IB Director are slated to visit the region. In Manipur, authorities recovered twelve weapons, killed a suspected KCP cadre, and handed over the bodies of villagers killed in an October attack after an agreement, while the state also sent spurious liquor samples to a laboratory for testing following a hooch-related deaths controversy. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker i Jammu og Kashmir gjennomfører høyt nivå-gjennomganger av vinter-sikkerhet og borger-sentrert politiarbeid, mens seks militante ble drept i nylige sammenstøt og senior-embetsmenn som innenrikssekretæren og IB-direktøren er planlagt å besøke regionen. I Manipur har myndighetene funnet tolv våpen, drept en mistenkt KCP-medarbeider, og overlevert likene til landsbyboere som ble drept i et angrep i oktober etter en avtale, mens staten også sendte falske spritprøver til et laboratorium for testing etter en kontrovers om dødsfall knyttet til hjemmelaget sprit. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
